projects.name: bentOS — This Portfolio
projects.shortDescription: The site you're on. A Next.js + Three.js portfolio with a 3D viewer, Matter.js BentoGrid, grounded chat assistant, and a boot-screen OS theme.
projects.description: bentOS is Kevin's personal portfolio, built as an interactive OS-themed surface rather than a static resume. Features include a boot splash gate, a procedural 3D cat in a Three.js viewer with LOD and FPS-aware perf, an infinite Matter.js-driven BentoGrid for /projects and /playground, a Gemini-backed chat assistant that only answers from grounded portfolio content, eight playable mini-games, and a long-form /scrollable view with a globe of life locations. Strict TypeScript, Tailwind CSS variables for theming, Vitest + Playwright tests, Lighthouse CI, and bundle-size budgets enforced on every PR. Content (projects, photos, talking points) is file-based JSON and rebuilt automatically by an update-portfolio agent skill.

projects.name: component-cop
projects.shortDescription: Chrome DevTools extension that audits React apps for component duplication, inconsistent styling, and hardcoded colors.
projects.description: component-cop is a Chrome DevTools extension that audits a running React app in real time. It flags component duplication (similar trees that could be consolidated), inconsistent styling across the page, and hardcoded color values that should be design tokens — giving frontend engineers a fast, in-browser way to find drift before it ships.

projects.name: clanker-spanker
projects.shortDescription: macOS desktop app that monitors GitHub pull requests and automatically fixes CI failures and code-review comments using Claude.
projects.description: clanker-spanker is a Tauri-based macOS desktop app that watches your GitHub PRs and automatically resolves blockers — CI failures, code-review comments, requested changes — by dispatching Claude with a curated context window for each PR. Reduces the manual round-trip between 'PR opened' and 'PR mergeable'.

projects.name: bento-ya
projects.shortDescription: Tauri desktop app for orchestrating AI coding agents — a kanban board where columns are pipeline stages with trigger-driven automation.
projects.description:
bento-ya is a Tauri desktop application for orchestrating AI coding agents through a kanban-style board. Each column is a pipeline stage with optional on_entry / on_exit triggers — describe the automation in natural language and the app generates the trigger config, or drop into an advanced editor for actions like spawn_cli, move_column, run_script, and create_pr.

Highlights:
- Per-task agent panel with embedded tmux-backed terminal, semantic transcript, lifecycle controls (Hold / Stop / Kill), and live model + thinking-effort selectors.
- v2.0 adds GitHub PR auto-create on column exit, per-task git worktree isolation, and a DAG dependency UI with hover-reveal bezier lines and cycle detection.
- v2.1 adds full per-task xterm.js terminals — WebGL renderer, 10k-line scrollback, Unicode 11, theme-reactive, lazy PTY sessions spawned on panel open.

projects.name: choomfie
projects.shortDescription: Personal AI agent powered by the Claude Code CLI — Discord, terminal, persistent memory, and a custom skill system.
projects.description:
choomfie is Kevin's personal AI agent built on top of the Claude Code CLI. It runs as a long-lived daemon that's reachable from Discord and a local terminal, with persistent memory across sessions and a pluggable skill system for invoking tools, services, and bespoke workflows.

Built as a multi-surface assistant rather than a one-off chatbot — Discord for casual conversation, terminal for power use, and a skill registry for deterministic actions.

projects.name: DeadInternetTheory
projects.shortDescription: Local-first marketing and content agent orchestrator — research, generate, approve, and publish across platforms with human-in-the-loop audit trails.
projects.description:
DeadInternetTheory is a local-first marketing and content-agent orchestrator. Users plug in a product or content lane, configure supervised marketing/content agents, research relevant communities and approved sources, then generate posts, scripts, images, voice/video assets — with human approval gates, dry-run scheduling, export, and publishing through owned or authorized social accounts.

Currently a pivoting MVP: FastAPI backend, Next.js frontend, Celery/Redis workers, Postgres models, tests, and extensive planning docs. The direction expands marketing operations into a full content-production pipeline with agent handoffs, source provenance, human approval, and audit trails.

projects.name: Slothing
projects.shortDescription: Open-source, privacy-first job-application command center. Build tailored resumes and cover letters, track opportunities, and prep for interviews — self-host free or use slothing.work.
projects.description:
Slothing is an open-source, privacy-first job-application assistant. Users upload career documents, build tailored resumes and cover letters in one workspace, track opportunities, and prepare for interviews — with AI doing the heavy lifting while their data stays under their control.

The product inverts the typical job-tool model: pay weekly only while actively searching ($6.99/week or $19.99/month on the hosted version at slothing.work), or self-host this repo for free forever. Hosted = same OSS code + a small proprietary billing module under an open-core split.

projects.name: TaserDerby
projects.shortDescription: Digital stakes, physical consequence. A derby-based betting mini-game that tases you when you lose.
projects.description:
TaserDerby pairs a single-player race-betting web app with a custom physical device that delivers a real (low-voltage) shock when you lose. It exists to make a point about the gap between digital risk and embodied consequence.

Built as two projects:
- The hardware controller (`TaserDerby` repo, C++) that drives the shock circuit.
- The web frontend (`TaserDerbyWebsite`, JavaScript) that runs the race and bet flow.

projects.name: Robotic Arm Puppeteer
projects.shortDescription: Python + ROS2 control and calibration toolkit for the OpenArm platform — multi-camera AprilTag perception, Dynamixel motor SDK integration, and a Flask + Three.js web UI for live calibration.
projects.description:
A Python + ROS2 based control and calibration toolkit for the OpenArm robotic platform, designed to make puppeteering, simulation, and data collection for sim training more intuitive, cost-effective, and accurate. It supports reading wrist joint positions, calibrating motion ranges, and integrates seamlessly with ROS2 for robotic simulation and control.

Highlights:
- Built a Python + ROS2 environment, integrating the Dynamixel motor SDK for encoder reading and writing through serial.
- Implemented a multi-camera AprilTag perception system using OpenCV ArUco with covariance-based accuracy filtering.
- Created an auto-calibration pipeline that generates reusable YAML configs for custom AprilTag bundle layouts.
- Bridged with ROS2 for teleoperation and visualization via Rviz2, MuJoCo, Isaac Sim, and MeshCat.
- Published fused 6DoF poses as ROS2 TF topics to support inverse kinematics and teleoperation downstream.
- Designed multiple ergonomic controllers and modular AprilTag mounts with print-in-place joints in Fusion 360.
- Configured and daisy-chained Dynamixel motors via U2D2 — unique IDs, voltage and current limits, the full bring-up.
- Built a local Flask + Three.js web tool for real-time encoder visualization, interactive calibration, and JSON storage.

projects.name: Expressive AI Robot Head
projects.shortDescription: ROS2 robotic head that fuses LLM reasoning, speech, vision, and 12-servo control to push AI from text into physical interaction.
projects.description:
A ROS2-based robotic head that integrates large language models (LLMs), speech, vision, and servo control to push AI beyond text into physical interaction — engaging more humanlike communication with AI through robots.

Highlights:
- Built a GPU-accelerated pipeline with CUDA and PyTorch, optimizing VRAM usage to run fully locally on Ubuntu/WSL2.
- Implemented a real-time speech workflow: Silero VAD → Whisper (STT) → llama.cpp (running GPT-OSS-20B) → Zonos (TTS).
- Designed a 12-servo robotic head combining organic mesh modeling in Blender with parametric solids in Fusion 360.
- Controlled servos through ROS2 with a mapping layer that unites LLM reasoning, audio analysis, and OpenCV tracking.
- Submitted as 'MaidReal Head' on Devpost.

projects.name: AR Gesture Controlled Robot
projects.shortDescription: Modular robot controlled through Snap Spectacles AR — finger gestures move and grab objects in the physical world with sub-100ms latency.
projects.description:
Built a modular robot platform controlled through Snap Spectacles, enabling natural gesture-based navigation and robotic-arm manipulation. Teleoperation feels as natural as moving your own hands.

Highlights:
- Developed an end-to-end gesture-to-motion pipeline: Snap API → Flask server → HiveMQ MQTT → ROS2 nodes.
- Implemented on NVIDIA Jetson Nano, handling motor drivers, camera streaming, and AI inference fully on-device.
- Created a Lens Studio AR application for gesture recognition and live camera streaming back to the AR glasses.
- Designed a mobile 2-wheel drive base with modular chassis attachments, including a 3DoF robotic arm.
- Optimized the system for sub-100ms latency and introduced an MQTT communication layer that scales to multi-robot scenarios.
- Submitted on Devpost as 'Kenesis'.

projects.name: PCB Design & Assembly
projects.shortDescription: Designed and routed double-layer PCBs in Altium Designer with zero ERC/DRC violations. Hand-assembled SMD boards including IMU and power-control circuits.
projects.description:
Picked up the full PCB design and assembly workflow — from schematic capture in Altium Designer through routing, fabrication review, and hand-assembly of SMD components.

Highlights:
- Onboarded by learning the process for developing a circuit board from start to finish in Altium Designer.
- Created a controller board's breakout for debugging, adding features like pull-ups for I²C communication lines.
- Sought mentorship from hardware leads to design the schematic with the correct components in Altium Designer.
- Cleanly routed all the ports utilizing vias and traces, resulting in 0 errors and uniform spacing throughout.
- Assembled and soldered PCBs (e.g. an IMU board) using surface-mount components, lead solder, and a hot plate.

projects.name: LitterCaching
projects.shortDescription: Geocaching, but you save the world. Environmental geocaching focused on litter collection — one cache at a time.
projects.description: LitterCaching reframes geocaching around an environmental goal: participants don't hunt hidden treasure, they hunt and collect litter. The app surfaces nearby litter hotspots, lets users log clean-ups, and gamifies environmental impact.

projects.name: ShoulderCupid
projects.shortDescription: Hackathon Winner — Cupid lost his bow, so he whispers the secrets of love directly in your ear. A wearable AI matchmaker.
projects.description: ShoulderCupid is a hackathon-winning wearable that puts a tiny 'shoulder cupid' on your shoulder, listening to the conversation and whispering AI-driven love advice in your ear in real time.

projects.name: SnapFire
projects.shortDescription: Hackathon Winner — never nap without having the Snap. A nap-timer application built for Snap devices.
projects.description: SnapFire is a nap-timer application built natively for Snap devices. It won its hackathon track for tight integration with the Snap platform and a focused, polished UX.

projects.name: One Handed Keyboard
projects.shortDescription: Wrist-mounted AAC keyboard with only 5 GPIO buttons, trie-based predictive text, and STM32 firmware over UART. Project submission received a 99% grade.
projects.description:
An AAC (augmentative and alternative communication) device in the form of a wrist-mounted keyboard, offering a more intuitive typing experience through simplified sequential input and predictive text for mobility-limited users.

Highlights:
- Designed a wrist-mounted keyboard with full functionality and autocorrect in software using only 5 GPIO buttons.
- Fabricated the housing using CAD software, ensuring structural stability when typing and adjustability for user comfort.
- Built and assembled a high-functioning transmitter, capable of transmitting data through UART over a meter long.
- Programmed and integrated system components using STM32Cube, with wiring plans made in Altium Designer.
- Combined a trie and fuzzy-search algorithm for an advanced word prediction system, allowing shortcuts for words.
- Project submission received an overall 99% grade with thorough written documentation.

projects.name: C# Apps & Games
projects.shortDescription: C# applications and Unity 2D/3D games — won Best Overall at UWGDC Game Jam Fall 2024. Includes computer-vision-driven projects and FSM-based gameplay.
projects.description:
A collection of C# work spanning vision-driven applications and Unity games — including the Best Overall winner at UWGDC Game Jam Fall 2024.

Highlights:
- Wrote C# code in Visual Studio 2022 using Emgu OpenCV as the computer-vision element for a larger alarm system.
- Developed complex game logic using C# scripting in Unity for 2D and 3D games (physics, colliders, AI logic).
- Utilized finite state machines for smooth animation transitions and character behaviour, leading to more interactivity.
- Employed version control (Git) to manage codebase changes and collaborate with teammates effectively.
- Conducted extensive testing and debugging to identify and fix issues, ensuring a polished final product.

projects.name: VR Haptic Gloves
projects.shortDescription: ESP32-based haptic gloves with spring-loaded potentiometers for finger position and servo-driven tactile feedback for VR emulation.
projects.description:
A pair of VR haptic gloves built from scratch — combining custom electronics, soldering, and 3D-printed fittings to give VR a real sense of touch.

Highlights:
- Soldered together an ESP32 with various electronic components, badge reels, 3D prints, and 22 AWG wire.
- Incorporated spring-loaded potentiometers to measure precise positioning of fingers, enabling emulation in VR.
- Utilized servos to create a haptic feedback system, providing realistic tactile responses based on virtual interactions.
- 3D-printed tailored custom fittings with a range of lightweight materials: PLA, TPU, and PETG.

projects.name: Java & Android Applications
projects.shortDescription: Android apps and Java utilities — CameraX object detection that web-scrapes decomposition times, an AIML chatbot with MBROLA text-to-speech, and Processing sketches.
projects.description:
A set of Java work across Android Studio, Eclipse, and Processing — combining CameraX-based real-time object detection, AIML chatbots, and natural-sounding speech synthesis.

Highlights:
- Made an Android Studio app that detects objects with CameraX and web-scrapes decomposition times from a database.
- Built an interactive chatbot using AIML (Artificial Intelligence Markup Language) for conversational logic in Eclipse IDE.
- Incorporated MBROLA and FreeTTS for natural-sounding speech synthesis, enhancing user interaction.
- Designed an intuitive interface for easy use and optimized for backwards compatibility on various Androids.

projects.name: FIRST Tech Challenge — Team Devolotics
projects.shortDescription: Lead builder and programmer for team Devolotics at the FIRST Tech Challenge World Championship. Built the drone launcher, deposit system, autonomous program, and CAD mechanisms.
projects.description:
Competed at the FIRST Tech Challenge World Championship as the lead builder and programmer for team Devolotics (19498).

Highlights:
- Main contributions toward Pluto's deposit system, gate opener, hang, drone launcher, and the autonomous program.
- Modeled various mechanisms using CAD, incorporating machined aluminum, polycarbonate, and 3D-printed components.
- Created a rubber-band-tensioned drone launcher with a latch mechanism and spring absorption using just a single servo.
- Programmed mecanum drive movement through splines and robot behaviour for an autonomous cycle.
